description_source: In supported regions, Computer Use in the ChatGPT desktop app is available on macOS and Windows with ChatGPT Work and Codex. Install the Computer Use plugin. On macOS, grant Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions when prompted.

Windows only: path to the Git Bash executable (bash.exe). Use when Git Bash is installed but not in your PATH. If the path doesn't exist or the file isn't named bash.exe, sh.exe, bash, or sh, Claude Code ignores the variable and auto-detects Git Bash as if it were unset, logging a warning visible with --debug. Before v2.1.219, Claude Code exited at startup when the path didn't exist, and used any existing file as the shell without checking that it was bash or sh. See Windows setup

Plugin directories to load for the session, each loaded the way a --plugin-dir flag loads it. Separate multiple paths with : on Unix or ; on Windows. Give each path as an absolute path or start it with ~, because Claude Code skips relative paths. Requires Claude Code v2.1.280 or later. See Load a plugin for one session

Set to 1 to stop Claude Code from passing -ExecutionPolicy Bypass when spawning PowerShell for tool calls, hooks, and status line commands, and respect the machine's effective execution policy instead. By default Claude Code bypasses execution policy at process scope so .ps1 scripts and module imports work on default-Restricted Windows installs. Process-scope bypass never overrides Group Policy MachinePolicy or UserPolicy regardless of this setting

Open the Claude Desktop app on the current directory and exit without starting a session in the terminal. Add --continue, or --resume with a session ID, to open that session in Desktop instead. --resume here takes only a session ID, not a name or transcript path. Takes no prompt and no other flags except --verbose and the --debug flags, since the app starts the session itself. Available on macOS and x64 Windows when you're signed in with a Claude subscription. Requires Claude Code v2.1.285 or later — claude --desktop

Let sandboxed commands on macOS send Apple Events, which open, osascript, and tools that open URLs in a browser need; without it they fail with error -600. This removes code-execution isolation: sandboxed commands can launch other applications unsandboxed with no user prompt, and can send AppleScript commands to running applications such as Terminal, subject to the per-app macOS automation-consent prompt (TCC).
Delete to end of word — Deletes to the end of the current word, or to the end of the next word when the cursor is between words. Stores deleted text for pasting. Requires Option as Meta on macOS

Delete back to previous whitespace — Stores deleted text for pasting. One press removes a whole path or --flag=value. To delete only the previous word, press Option+Delete on macOS or Ctrl+Backspace on Windows
Continue the current session in the ChatGPT desktop app. — Move from the TUI to the desktop app on macOS or Windows.
Grant sandbox read access to an extra directory (Windows only). — Unblock commands that need to read an absolute directory path outside the current readable roots.
Set up the elevated agent sandbox (Windows only). — Replace the degraded Windows sandbox after Codex offers the elevated setup.
Workspace path for the ChatGPT desktop app. On macOS, Codex opens this path; on Windows, Codex prints the path. (valeurs : path)

Type : boolean. Prefer MXC for local Windows execution when native capabilities and policy allow it; otherwise retain the configured legacy sandbox and setup. Disabled by default in the standalone CLI; the desktop app can enable it through rollout configuration. Command failures don't trigger fallback.
Type : boolean. Use the unified PTY-backed exec tool (stable; enabled by default except on Windows).
Record & Replay is available on macOS. Computer Use must also be available and enabled.
